chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Jamil, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him: Does the return (raj'ah) occur without sexual intercourse? He said: Yes.

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the narrator of this ruling.
key_terms.الرِّجْعَةُ: The right of a husband to take back his wife during the 'iddah (waiting period) after a revocable divorce.

ai.seo_question: Does a husband need to have sexual intercourse with his wife to validly exercise the right of Raj'ah during the divorce waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies a specific nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the revocable divorce (talaq raj'i), confirming that physical consummation is not a prerequisite for the husband to exercise the right of 'raj'ah' during the 'iddah. This ruling underscores the legal validity of the marital bond remaining intact solely through the initial contract and pronouncement, allowing for reconciliation without the need for a new nikah. It highlights the flexibility within the 'iddah period for restoring the previous marital status, a key distinction from the irrevocable divorce (talaq ba'in).
